questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was possible to take classes in English and French. The international selection of courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
As I am in law, this will be reflected throughout the evaluation.
I enjoyed my time at Université de Genève as to why extended my exchange. I found the courses within international law, Geneva’s international buzz etc. very appealing. There are lots of courses and other events related to international law, politics etc. Also, I wanted to further improve my French.
The University offers a Certificate in Transnational Law (CTL). It is worth considering. Depending on the courses that you take, you can obtain the certificate.
You can read more about the CTL here:
https://www.unige.ch/droit/transnational/certificat
https://www.unige.ch/droit/transnational/professeurs/enseignements

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find the needed information upon my arrival. Université de Genève as well as UCPH was very organized when it came to providing the needed information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a mandatory orientation meeting explaining all the necessary information. We were as well provided with a nice flyer with a step-by-step overview of all the things we needed to complete.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I couldn’t have been more satisfied with the help and orientation provided by Université de Genève. It was super organized, and everyone was very helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Student accommodation is offered to some extent, however, it is scarce. 
I applied as soon as it was possible and I was lucky to get a dorm room. If you are offered a place, please be aware of the rather short time limit to accept. I had 48 hours to accept.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It is generally very difficult to find housing in Geneva. Due to the demand for housing, the rent tends to be quite high if you do not find any student housing.
You can read more about the housing here:
https://www.unige.ch/batiment/service-batiments/logements/en/

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The first week or so of classes, it is possible to try all the different classes that you might be interested in. I found this very nice, as it gives an opportunity to try the classes before choosing them. I didn’t buy the books/polycopié before after choosing. However, it was still possible to look through some of the material, as it is shared on Moodle too (corresponding to Absalon).

The course registration process is a two-step process, first you register for the courses. Later, you register for the exams. Everything is done through the university’s ‘portail’. It is very important that the courses you want to take and do the exam in, is registered twice (both the course registration and later the exam registration as well). As mentioned, you will be well informed about this multiple times.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The process of registering for courses at University de Genève is explained during the mandatory orientation meeting, in the flyer with the step-by-step overview and during the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
It is my understanding that you can register with all the classes within the Faculty of Law. However, there are some ‘seminars’ where UNIGE students have priority as these are mandatory for their memoire (master thesis).

It is possible to take courses at different faculties - and institutes (as a part of the CTL). I took all my classes at the Faculty of Law as to why I have no experience with this. It was, however, once again well explained by Université de Genève.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to register for the courses and exams respectively. If courses and exams are taken as a part of the CTL, they should be registered specifically for this. It is explained once you get to the university. 

Be aware, the CTL must be applied for separately. This can be done even before you arrive in Geneva.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I very much appreciated the selection within international law. The professors had a lot of relevant practical experience, usually from one of the international organizations located in Geneva.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Generally, I found the level of the courses to be easier than the once at UCPH, when considering the grading. 

However, the level of the courses differs depending on which of the courses you chose. To my understanding, the professors have a lot of autonomy to choose the type of exam etc. Some exams are multiple choice, for example. These are obviously easier. Others are open or closed books. I recommend that you double check with the professor how the examination is, it is usually explained during the first class, but it is not always clear.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Like at UCPH, you usually only have two hours of class per course per week. They estimate four hours of preparation for each class. I used more time than that. Most courses are six ECTS meaning that you will have to take five classes (30 ECTS). I found that to quite a lot in the beginning, but I got used to it some weeks in. I found it to be nice being able to do multiple courses.  

Most of the classes are lectures, not case work as it is at UCPH. Once again, it depends on the course. Most courses are recorded, and it is thereby possible to rewatch them after class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative Methodology: Contract Law 
WTO Law and Practice
Practice of International Humanitarian Law 
European Competition Law 
Organisation internationale (in French) 
Twi French language courses (no credits)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I can especially recommend WTO Law and Practice and Practice of International Humanitarian Law (IHL). I found the professors to be very knowledgeable within their field. For IHL, I signed up for the optional pleading. I pleaded with a German girl on a provided topic. The topic was the naval blockade imposed on Paletstine, by Israel. It was very interesting to work this practically with the conflict. It was a bit demanding, but when you did the pleading, you were only examined on International Armed Conflicts (part I of the course), and not Non-International Armed Conflicts (part II of the course). 

Furthermore, I can recommend Organisation Internatioanle. Challenge yourself by taking a course in French. Improving your French in Geneva is rather difficult, as a lot of people are international students, and/or speak English. I found it difficult in the beginning, I understood almost nothing, but this improved rather quickly. Most courses are recorded so that you can rewatch them on Mediaserver. Alternatively, you can choose a course you have already had before and thereby know. Like the Internal Market of the European Union (Droit du marché intérieur de l'Union européenne).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is more expensive to buy groceries and to eat and drink out. In general, Geneva is a quite expensive city.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of different sports and cultural activities offered through the university. The student associations are very active and happy to welcome you.
Some of them are free. Others are offered at student friendly prices.
You can read more about it here:
https://vie-de-campus.unige.ch/sport-culture/sport
and here
https://www.unige.ch/dife/culture/
.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I volunteered at the Croix-Rouge genevoise with an elderly lady two hours a week as well as at retirement home once a month. I had a lovely time. It was furthermore a really good way of getting insight in the Swiss culture, meeting locals and improving my French.
You can read more about it here:
https://www.croix-rouge-ge.ch/nos-activites
Even though my level of French was not very good and I couldn’t commit to the commitment period stated, they allowed me to start. As I was ensured through Croix-Rouge when I took part in the activities, I did not need a separate insurance.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
It is easy to get around Switzerland by train. Personally, I was interested in experiencing the four different languages spoken and how the culture differed in the different regions. I travelled with an interrail ticket, but you can also get some ‘supersaver tickets’ for a decent price. The nature is wonderful. I really enjoyed hiking.
You can check out this website and sign up for the newsletter to get recommendations on what to do in Geneva:
https://www.geneve.ch
I participated in the ESN intraweek. It was a nice way to meet other exchange students. They also give you a good introduction to the city, university etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to adjust. Geneva is a wealthy and safe city. In many ways it reminds me of Copenhagen in that regard. Stores and restaurants close quite early and a lot of places are closed on Sundays. Applications etc. are mostly made by mail, not online.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I joined Croix-Rouge and talked to students in the different classes that I had. Do not be scared to initiate the conversation. Join a team sport or the musical.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Swiss people are very polite. I was very curious about the society; direct democracy, the cantonal differences etc. Geneva is particular for its international environment.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Université de Genève is a very good university both academically and regarding its activities (cultural and sports as well as student associations). 

Make use of free French classes. The sooner you sign up for the language classes, the greater chance there is to get your preferred class. 

Go and explore Switzerland while you are there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting wonderful people and finding my path academically and professionally. Experiencing Geneva’s international vibe. I found it to be very stimulating.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Prioritizing my money wisely ;)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go - you will not regret it! Bon courage!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
